section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch1 — Baumrind's Parenting Styles
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Parents who set clear, high expectations and firm rules for their child, but also explain the reasoning behind rules, remain warm and responsive, and encourage open discussion, are displaying which of Baumrind's parenting styles — generally associated with the best child outcomes?
explanation: Authoritative parenting combines high demands with high warmth and responsiveness — linked to the best outcomes among Baumrind's four parenting styles.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch1 — Baumrind's Parenting Styles
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Parents who demand strict, unquestioning obedience to rules, offer little warmth or explanation, and rely on punishment for enforcement ('because I said so') are displaying which of Baumrind's parenting styles?
explanation: Authoritarian parenting is high on demands/control but low on warmth and responsiveness — rules enforced strictly with little explanation.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch1 — Baumrind's Parenting Styles
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Parents who are warm and loving but set very few rules or expectations, rarely enforcing consequences and letting the child largely regulate their own behaviour, are displaying which of Baumrind's parenting styles?
explanation: Permissive (indulgent) parenting is high on warmth but low on demands/control — few rules or consequences.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch1 — Baumrind's Parenting Styles
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Parents who are emotionally detached, provide minimal supervision, and show little interest or involvement in their child's daily life or activities are displaying which of Baumrind's parenting styles — generally linked to the poorest child outcomes?
explanation: Neglectful (uninvolved) parenting is low on BOTH warmth and demands — associated with the poorest outcomes among Baumrind's four parenting styles.
